Vector Search

an5 ORM includes built-in vector search capabilities for AI and machine learning applications.

Overview

Vector search allows you to find similar items based on semantic meaning rather than exact matches. This is useful for:

  • Semantic search in documentation
  • Recommendation systems
  • Image similarity search
  • Natural language queries

Choosing a backend

The TypeScript runtime tries the backends in this order and uses the first one that works. Other runtimes have their own provider support; use the examples for your stack below.

Order Backend Needs
1 NBase — Neural Vector Database An NBase endpoint
2 PostgreSQL pgvector extension
3 SQL Server 2025 VECTOR_DISTANCE
4 In-memory Nothing, but the whole table is loaded

Use NBase when the embedding table is too large to scan: the vectors live in the vector database and the rows stay in your table, so a search never loads the table into memory.

Examples for your stack

Selected: rust / sqlserver.

Native search requires SQL Server 2025 VECTOR_DISTANCE and compatible embeddings. Earlier versions use the in-memory fallback.

Generate the Document model client first and configure its adapter for the selected provider. The snippets assume an initialized runtime table client named table (or a generated TypeScript client named db) and a query embedding with the same dimension as stored embeddings.

use an5_adapters::VectorSearchArgs;

let results = table.vector_search(&VectorSearchArgs {
    vector: query_embedding,
    take: 10,
    vector_field: "embedding".into(),
    distance_metric: "cosine".into(),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;

Use the adapter source in an5Adapters/rust as a local Cargo path dependency until registry availability is verified.

Advanced NBase and relation examples are available in the TypeScript reference.
